Observed:
- Painless right testicular swelling
- Enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
- Bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement
- 82-year-old man
- Painless right testicular swelling of several weeks’ duration
- No systemic symptoms
- History of glaucoma, prostatic adenomectomy, and hernioplasty
- Medications: dorzolamide, lansoprazole, and dutasteride
- Testicular ultrasound showed enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
- Ipsilateral hydrocele
- Swelling persisted after 10 days of amoxicillin–clavulanate
- Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT confirmed testicular pathology
- New bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement
- Adrenal nodules were absent on a CT scan 3 years earlier
- 18 FDG PET/CT showed intense uptake in the right testis
- No uptake in the adrenal glands
- Normal laboratory evaluation
- Negative serologies for active HCV and EBV
- Positive for past EBV
Differential diagnosis:
1. Leydig cell tumor
2. Testicular lymphoma
3. Seminoma
4. Adrenal metastasis from testicular cancer
5. Testicular sex cord-stromal tumor
